claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
Casting or equivalent processing can produce the stated intrinsic hierarchical microstructure in HfNbTiVAl10.
SEM or EBSD imaging can capture the distribution and connectivity of the relevant heterostructural features.
A machine-learning surrogate can use multiscale microstructural descriptors to predict elastic modulus.
A machine-learning surrogate can use multiscale microstructural descriptors to predict yield strength.
A machine-learning surrogate can use multiscale microstructural descriptors to predict fracture metrics.
The distributions of phases, grain boundaries, and interfaces are key features governing the mechanical properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
The hierarchical interfaces mediate load transfer.
The hierarchical interfaces promote or govern crack deflection.
Linking high-resolution microstructural features to mechanical response with machine learning can bypass the computational complexity of full-scale finite-element or crystal-plasticity simulations.
Correlations between local interface characteristics and global mechanical response can maintain or improve predictive accuracy.
The surrogate model will be at least 5–10 times faster than established simulation frameworks.
The surrogate model will reduce prediction error for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture parameters by at least 5–10% relative to established simulations.
Conventional finite-element or crystal-plasticity models use averaged material properties and omit detailed multiscale heterostructural information.
Poorly resolved or excessively complex heterostructural features may prevent robust surrogate-model inputs.
Unrepresented casting defects or porosity may dominate mechanical response and reduce predictive performance.
Prediction-speed and accuracy gains depend on dataset extent and quality.
Prediction-speed and accuracy gains depend on model architecture and training regimen.

contradictions.description: The baseline defines conventional simulations as using averaged properties and omitting detailed heterostructural information, whereas the validation design refers to standard, detailed physics-based simulations. These may not be the same comparator.

The hypothesis requires the surrogate to be both faster and more accurate, but the falsification rule requires failure of both the speed and accuracy thresholds. Under that rule, failure on only one required advantage would not decisively falsify the conjunctive hypothesis.
